questions.prompt: What is the primary indicator in a database query execution plan that a full table scan is being performed instead of utilizing an index?
questions.explanation: A sequential or table scan indicates the database is reading every row in the table sequentially, which is often a sign of a missing index.

questions.prompt: You notice an application making 1 query to fetch a list of 50 users, followed by 50 individual queries to fetch each user's profile details. What performance anti-pattern is this?
questions.explanation: The N+1 query problem occurs when an application executes 1 initial query to retrieve a parent list, and then N additional queries to retrieve related child records individually.

questions.prompt: When designing a composite index on columns (A, B, C) for a table, which of the following query WHERE clauses will NOT effectively utilize this index?
questions.explanation: B-tree composite indexes follow a left-prefix rule. A query skipping the leading column (A) and querying only (B, C) cannot fully leverage the index.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the most effective way to eliminate an N+1 query problem when fetching parent records and their associated child records?

options.text: Increase the database connection pool size.
Add a unique index to the child table foreign key.
Use a JOIN or eager loading mechanism to fetch data in a single query.
Enable query caching on the application server.

questions.explanation: Eager loading or using a SQL JOIN combines the retrieval of parent and child records into one or a controlled constant number of queries, avoiding the N+1 loop.

questions.prompt: Looking at a query execution plan, you see a 'Nested Loop' operating on a large table with 1,000,000 rows without an index on the join condition, resulting in very high execution time. What is the most appropriate fix?

options.text: Add an index on the join column of the inner table.
Increase the database memory allocation for sorting.
Change the query to use an OFFSET pagination method.
Disable nested loops globally in the database configuration.

questions.explanation: A nested loop without an index forces a full scan of the inner table for every row of the outer table. Adding an index allows the inner table lookups to use index scans.

questions.prompt: An application frequently queries a table using both a range condition on a timestamp column and an equality condition on a status column (e.g., WHERE status = 'active' AND created_at > ?). How should you construct a composite index to optimize this query?

options.text: Two separate indexes: one on status, one on created_at
Index on (status) and a functional index on created_at

questions.explanation: Equality columns should generally come first in a composite index so the B-tree can immediately jump to the exact subset of rows, leaving the range column second to narrow down the remaining results.
